title: Dimension of local components under weakly etale maps from a universally catenary domain
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], universally catenary in the sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $K$ be its fraction field, and suppose that the integral closure $\overline C$ of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring, and let $f:C\to D$ be a local weakly etale homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], where local means $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)=\mathfrak m_C$. For every minimal prime ideal $P$ of $D$, one has $\dim(D/P)=\dim C$, with Krull dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A minimal prime is a prime containing no strictly smaller prime. A local ring has exactly one maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero and has no zero divisors.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

proof.text: Put A=D/P, C' equal to the normalization of C, H=C' tensor_C D, and E equal to the normalization of A. The normalization tensor decomposition [lem-exc-weakly-etale-normalization-tensor] supplies a surjection t:H->E compatible with D. Base change of finite module generators makes H finite over D, and the D-linear projection makes E finite over D and hence over A. The integral injective inclusions give dim E=dim A and dim C'=dim C by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal].

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

proof.text: The map C'->H is weakly etale by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]. The proved bound [lem-exc-weakly-etale-dimension-upper-bound] gives dim H<=dim C'. Surjective prime contraction embeds chains of E into chains of H, so dim E<=dim H (Mathlib ringKrullDim_le_of_surjective). Thus dim A<=dim C. No finite-dimension assertion or maximal-length chain is needed.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

proof.text: Choose any maximal ideal n of E using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]; E is a domain. Let g:C'->E be the composite through H and put m=n comap g. The product projection E times F->E is localization away from (1,0) (Mathlib Prod.away_fst), hence flat. Both normalization equivalences preserve flatness, and C'->H is weakly etale and therefore flat. Composition makes g flat. The canonical local map C'_m->E_n is flat (Mathlib RingHom.Flat.localRingHom).

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

proof.text: Since E is finite over the local ring A, n contracts to the maximal ideal of A [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]. The surjective quotient map D->A is local. Compatibility of t and the original local map f shows that m contracts to the maximal ideal of C. Finiteness of C' over C implies integrality [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so m is maximal by integral incomparability [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability]. The finite-normalization dimension theorem [lem-exc-weakly-etale-normalization-dimension] gives dim C'_m=dim C.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

proof.text: The flat local map C'_m->E_n is faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective]. Thus [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-local-dimension] gives dim C=dim C'_m<=dim E_n. The chains-below-prime description [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] bounds dim E_n by dim E=dim A. Combine with the upper bound of Step 2.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

Greco is not in literature/ and network access is blocked, so I could not reopen it. Instead I checked the item's truth through the full 7-step proof. Step 1: the tensor node's hypotheses are exactly the item's, and E is finite over D/P because the generators descend. Step 2: dim E_n = dim A, using integral-injective dimension, finite local dimension, maximal ideal existence and chains-below-prime; no catenarity of A is used. Step 3: the idempotent projection is a localization, so C'_m->E_n is a weakly étale base change and local; locality is claimed only after localizing. Step 4: n∩A = m_A, so m∩C = m_C, and m is maximal by incomparability. Step 5: flat local map, so faithfully flat, so dim R <= dim S. Step 6: the fibre over a field is weakly étale with integral elements (092Q), so fibre primes are incomparable and the inclusion-preserving fibre bijection gives dim S <= dim R. Step 7 is elementary. New node normalization-tensor is true: I checked it via Stacks 092W lemma-normality-goes-up (more-algebra.tex:30728, read) plus Q(D) = K⊗D reduced and zero-dimensional, then the product splitting over minimal primes. It is not derivable in 2–3 lines and is not a duplicate. New node normalization-dimension: Stacks 02IJ (algebra.tex:27520, read) with transcendence degree 0 and a finite residue extension. Universal catenarity is genuinely needed (Nagata example). Small cases checked: a DVR with its strict henselization, the nodal local ring with its henselization (semilocal C'), and a field.
